what_happened: The design job "Revise warm-baseline design note to cover the CI-result path" was rejected at the final verdict. The verifier found 1 of 7 acceptance criteria unmet and 4 blocker or major findings. The unmet criterion required the Problem section to give measured durations for the CI-reuse and local-run paths from recorded jobs or THROUGHPUT.md, with a source for each number, estimates labeled, and the share of jobs that run checks locally. The note instead said the 14.1-minute median is mostly CI wait, which the records contradict. It gave the CI path as a guess of 8 to 15 minutes plus one October sample, though 52 measured CI run durations were in the records. Its headline recommendation was to restore the target cache on pull-request branches and split test across jobs, which the CI workflow already does. The verifier also found that the reading did not match the request, so passing criteria did not show the request was met. No failed checks were listed.
cause: Design jobs have no required step that inventories the current system and its recorded data before the doc proposes a change. Nothing makes the writer read the CI workflow and query the job records for measured durations, or compare each recommendation to what already exists. The reading and planning stages accept the request's framing as fact, so a note built on guesses and remembered assumptions looks complete. The criteria ask for sourced numbers, but nothing checks them before the verifier reads the repo at the end. This is the fourth case of the same gap.
prevention: Add a required "current state" step to every design job that changes an existing flow. Before drafting, the producer must write an inventory: the existing code, workflow and config for the area, each cited by file and function or step. It must also pull the relevant measured data from the job records, and every number must carry its source or an explicit "estimate" label. The planning critic must reject a plan with no inventory. A code check must refuse a design doc whose recommendations are not each tagged "new" or "already present" against that inventory. A second code check must refuse a Problem section whose numbers lack a source or estimate label. The reading stage must also restate the request and the inventory facts it relies on, so a misread request shows up before the producer starts.
proposed_request:
Revise docs/design/warm-baseline-build.md so it covers both the CI-result path and the local-run path. Outcome: a design note whose analysis rests on the system as it is today and on measured data.

1. Before proposing anything, add a short "Current state" section. It lists what the CI workflow and the local check path already do, including whether the target cache is restored on pull-request branches and whether test is split across jobs. Cite the workflow file and step names.
2. In the Problem section, give measured durations for the CI-reuse path and the local-run path from recorded jobs (ci_result source and duration fields) or from THROUGHPUT.md. Use the recorded CI run durations rather than a guessed range. Give the source of every number, label any unmeasured number as an estimate, and state what share of jobs run checks locally.
3. Check the claim that the 14.1-minute median is mostly CI wait against the recorded data. Correct or remove it.
4. Make every recommendation either a new change or marked as already present. Drop or rewrite any recommendation that the current workflow already implements. Base the remaining recommendation on the measured cause.
5. Keep the change to this one doc and its changelog entry, and do not use banned words.

Acceptance: each number in the Problem section names its source or says estimate. The note states the local-run share. No recommendation describes something the workflow already does.
